title: Volume-aware pager smoothing to stabilize SLO burn noise during capacity events
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We see repeated SLO burn-rate spikes during short-lived capacity congestion and autoscaler oscillation that generate high-volume paging. Current burn-rate alerts are too sensitive to short spikes and do not account for cluster headroom or request volume. This ticket implements a volume-aware pager smoothing layer with capacity-sensitive thresholds and a temporary circuit breaker to reduce noisy on-call interruptions while preserving detection of real regressions.

Background:
- Incidents (see incident-2026-02-05 and incident-2026-02-13) show bursts where burn rate crosses P1 thresholds for 2-5 minutes before autoscaler or fallback reduces load.
- Pager burn contributes to fatigue; many pages are duplication of same root cause (lack of dedup keys) and would be handled by existing runbooks if batched.

Proposal (mechanics):
1) Volume-aware smoothing: compute burn-rate with a weighted moving average that respects request volume. Small absolute-error spikes with low request volume should have less weight when triggering pagers.
2) Capacity-sensitive thresholds: scale burn thresholds by measured cluster headroom (% GPUs available) and recent autoscaler events. When headroom < 15% temporarily increase burn threshold (configurable multiplier) to avoid paging for transient overloads.
3) Short-circuit circuit breaker: when a capacity event (autoscaler scale-up/scale-down or known fleet rollout) is detected, enable an elevated suppression window (default 10m) with an escalator that tightens after sustained violation.
4) Dedup and impact-weighting: deduplicate alerts by root-cause fingerprint and weight them by customer impact to avoid paging for localized low-impact bursts.
5) Synthetic alert classifier (probabilistic): a light classifier uses volume, headroom, and recent rollout flags to tag low-confidence burn spikes for silent logging rather than paging. This is roll-forwarded behind a flag and will start as a trial.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Design RFC and config knobs (this ticket): finalize multipliers, decay windows, and API for headroom signal ingestion. (owner: Marcus)
- Instrument headroom telemetry and autoscaler event stream into alerting service (owner: infra team)
- Implement smoothing and suppression logic in alert router (PR #4123) and add dedup keys. (owner: eng-alerting)
- Add classifier model as a small rule-based/probabilistic function; provide opt-out per-service in console. (owner: ML infra)
- Dashboard: suppressed-alerts viewer, suppression reasons, and per-service suppressed count per day. (owner: observability)

Telemetry & metrics to add:
- suppressed_pager_count by reason (smoothing, headroom, circuit-breaker)
- burn_rate_raw vs burn_rate_smoothed time series
- headroom_percentage and recent_autoscaler_events stream
- time-to-first-un-suppressed-page for escalated incidents

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag default OFF globally. Enable for non-critical sandbox services (canary) for 48 hours.
- Evaluate suppressed pages and missed incidents for canary services against manual checks and postmortem expectations.
- Gradually expand to tier-2 services, then tier-1 after validation (approx 3 weeks).

Acceptance criteria (summary in separate field):
- 50% reduction in pages caused by sub-5 minute low-volume burn spikes in canary group after 1 week
- No customer-visible increase in undetected regressions during canary (manual checks + synthetic traffic)
- New dashboards emitting expected metrics and links in runbook

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: suppressing a real regression. Mitigation: conservative multipliers, short canary windows, escape hatch to disable smoothing per-service, and immediate hard thresholds that always page for very-high-impact customers.
- Risk: classifier false negatives. Mitigation: classifier initially flags (silent) instead of suppressing for first 72 hours and runs in shadow mode.

Runbook updates:
- Update SRE runbook with new suppression reasons, how to toggle per-service flags, and procedures to forcibly escalate if suppression hides a true outage.

Notes:
- This ticket ties into ENG-21459 (prevent burn pager cascade from autoscaler oscillation) and ENG-31204 (mitigate pager fatigue via burn-window tuning). Intends to produce both short-term relief and long-term policy knobs for alerting fidelity.

comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha: Created ticket after postmortem for incident-2026-02-13. Initial RFC draft posted to confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SLO/volume-aware-pager-smoothing

2026-02-25 - Marcus: Design review with alerting/infra/observability teams. Agreed multipliers: headroom threshold 15%, initial suppression multiplier 1.5x, smoothing window 90s with 3m decay. Action: infra to provide headroom stream (ENG-731460).

2026-03-01 - Marcus: PR #4123 created to add smoothing kernel and dedup keys into alert-router (https://github.com/redwood-inference/alert-router/pull/4123). Unit tests added for smoothing kernel edge-cases.
2026-03-05 - QA: Started shadow runs on staging for 48hrs, classifier in shadow mode. Observability: suppressed_pager_count metric emitted to staging Grafana dashboard (dashboard id: 785).

2026-03-10 - SRE: Canary rollout plan approved. First canary group (sandbox services) scheduled for 2026-03-14 behind feature flag. Ops will monitor headroom and will have immediate rollback script if undetected problems observed.
2026-03-13 - Marcus: Minor tweak after staging: increase smoothing kernel alpha for very low volume traffic to avoid under-weighting (PR #4160). Preparing release notes and runbook edits.
